newsitem.title: FRANCE: New French AIDS campaign aims to renew concern.
newsitem.headline: New French AIDS campaign aims to renew concern.

text.p: France's Health Department, fearing complacency will set in because of recent advances in AIDS treatment, has embarked on a new AIDS awareness campaign using advertising agency Australie.

The wide-ranging campaign, detailed last week by the Health Department, includes two series of television spots, a series of magazine advertisements to run over four months, and radio broadcasts, posters and information leaflets aimed at holiday-makers, the gay community, drug users and young people.
The Health Department said new therapies had marked the current phase of the AIDS epidemic.
"These therapies, which offer fantastic hope, also present the risk of reversing advances in prevention and in solidarity with those affected," the department said in a statement on the campaign.

The first television spot, which ran for 10 days in June, showed a man driving along a winding road in the dark and rain, who lets his attention wander because everything is going fine and finishes up in a ditch.

The second television series, running from July 21 until the end of September, aims to boost support for those infected by showing three social situations where a person has difficulty saying he or she is HIV-positive.
The magazine adverts, continuing the old-style message of prevention at every kind of sexual encounter, are running from July 21 to end-November.
A spokeswoman for Australie, part of ad network Euro RSCG, which has run the government's AIDS awareness campaigns for the last three years, declined to give the current campaign's budget.
